trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun (Case No.238 of 2008)
case_name: Sri Vineet Kumar Jain vs Smt. Archana Garg
facts_of_case: Married couple with two children; husband filed petition for divorce or judicial separation due to wife's behavior and conduct.

legal_principles.principle: Mere trivial irritations, quarrels, normal wear and tear of the married life which happens in day to day life would not be adequate for grant of divorce on the ground of mental cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The court held that mere trivial irritations, quarrels, or normal wear and tear of the married life are not sufficient grounds for granting a divorce based on mental cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: The married life should be reviewed as a whole and a few isolated instances over a period of years will not amount to cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The court held that the married life should be viewed as a whole, and isolated incidents over time do not constitute mental cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty is dependable to various factors. It is not an abstract principle.
legal_principles.held: The court held that mental cruelty depends on various factors and is not an abstract concept.

legal_principles.principle: Unilateral decision of refusal to have intercourse for considerable period without there being any physical incapacity or valid reason may amount to mental cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The court held that a spouse's unilateral decision to refuse sexual relations for an extended period, absent physical disability or a valid reason, can constitute mental cruelty.

outcome.final_order: Decree of judicial separation under Section 10 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 granted; counterclaim for custody of children decreed.
